column2: Markandeya said: Hearing this hymn of the great-souled Brahma, the god Krishna, lying in yoga-sleep, was awakened by Shri.
Seeing all the gods, of many forms and terrified, he said: "What has befallen you, that you have come here wishing to see me?"
Brahma spoke to Keshava, O Bharata: "Without you, lord of the world, who is our protector here from the thorns of the gods?
The earth is surrounded by danavas and heaven destroyed; sacrifices for dharma, desire and the rest, and the Vedas too, have been swept away.
Overwhelmed by the weight of the Danu-born, the earth has gone down to Rasatala. Jatasura, the daitya Jabali and the son of Maya —
ten crores of daityas, endowed with complete strength, possessed of Shiva's grace, causing the overthrow of heaven.
Therefore set your discus in motion and raise up your earth." Hearing this speech, afflicted by fear and pained in life, the god
said: "Give up the fear born of the daityas; in a short time I shall slay the great asuras."
Assuming the form of the Boar, he entered the water of the Kalpaga; he held the earth on the tip of his tusk and destroyed the danavas.
Creation was set going again just as before; the gods headed by Brahma, delighted, returned to heaven.
This I have told you, O king, of the Boar on the bank of the Kalpaga; by hearing and reciting it one gains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
The linga named Devapatha is saluted by gods and asuras; seeing it with faith brings the supreme goal to the ancestors.
In the month of Chaitra, on the fourteenth of both fortnights, all the holy places went there to bathe and to perform worthy rites.
That which is desired by the gods in the world of the gods, O banner of kings — thousands of lords of sages worship Shiva there,
some devoted to the chandrayana, others to the brahmakurcha, living on bulbs, roots and fruits, living on water, delighting in water,
ever devoted to the agnihotra and offering into the fire; they worship Devapatha and have attained supreme perfection.
Now I shall tell of another holy place that destroys sin, the supreme Sahasrayajna, giving the fruit of all desires.
Worshipping Janardana there on the eleventh of Margashirsha, a man obtains the fruit of having performed a thousand sacrifices.
He does not see Yama's world nor go into animal births; by the power of this holy place a man is freed of impurity.
This I have told you, O king, the unsurpassed holy account; by hearing and reciting it one is honoured in Vishnu's world.
Then one should go to Shuklatirtha, auspicious and containing all holy places, where by merely bathing a man gains the fruit of ten cows.
By it the gods Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshvara were made white; a crore and a quarter of holy places are established at Shuklatirtha.
Shuklatirtha measures eight cubits, Yudhishthira; there are Kalagnirudra, Shrikantha and another,
who attained supreme perfection there by their various fierce austerities; by the power of Shuklatirtha the gods rejoice in heaven.
Shakra too bathed the god of gods, husband of Uma, lord of the cities, with the water of the Reva and worshipped him with bilva leaves.
On the full moon and the new moon the Moon and Sun bathed there at Prabhavati together with the planets and the spheres of stars and the pole;
thereby the gods shine, by the power of Shuklatirtha. The holy hermitage of Kashyapa is frequented by gods and siddhas;
ten thousand sages dwell there in person, O Bharata, living on bulbs, roots and fruits, others living on water,
others on vegetables, others fasting, others practising the brahmakurcha, some devoted to the chandrayana, others fasting for a month.
Thirty-three crores of sages worship Shukleshvara. When the moon is seized by Rahu, and on the full-moon day,
all the holy places come to bathe here — this was spoken by Shiva. Whatever fruit there would be at Sthaneshvara at the conjunction of Rahu and the sun,
that whole fruit one obtains at Shuklatirtha, no doubt. Those who give golden cows, land and the like, silver and elephants —
giving these here, great king, there is no counting the merit. By Kubera the giver of wealth and by gods, gandharvas and danavas,
at the conjunction of Rahu and the sun, Maheshvara at Shuklatirtha was worshipped with sandal, aloe, camphor and garlands of flowers,
with canopies and fine banners and the lighting of rows of lamps; by the power of this holy place the king of yakshas became lord of wealth,
and by it the gods in heaven obtained enjoyments of many kinds. This holy place contains all holy places and all gods;
even in a thousand years the gods cannot complete the description of Shuklatirtha, in the Purana proclaimed by Skanda.
One gone into a sinful birth, one gone into an animal birth, the slayer of a brahmin, the drinker of liquor, the eater of Shiva's leftover offerings —
each is freed from that sin by the power of this holy place. A man who bathes there and worships the bull-bannered one
is worshipped by all the hosts of gods and asuras, best of men. This I have told you, O king, which destroys the great sins,
where long ago the Grandsire worshipped the lord of sacrifice at a sacrifice. Having composed a hymn duly to the god of gods, the trident-bearer,
and having worshipped Shukleshvara, Brahma uttered the hymn: "Salutation to Shiva, the tranquil, whose form is knowledge and realization;
to the subtle, of subtle form, subtle in all, the cause; to the subtle even among the subtle, salutation to the most subtle.
To the divine, of divine form, of divine body, the bridge; to the divine even among the divine, salutation to the most divine.
To the one with the lustre of the sky, to Being, to Aghora, salutation again and again; to the one whose abode has the measure of the sky, to Vamesha, salutation again and again.
To the Supreme, the supreme lord, the cause of the highest truth; to the supreme, the supremely free, salutation to the one beyond the supreme.
Salutation to you of one tongue, of two tongues, of many tongues, and likewise of countless tongues; to the three-eyed, salutation again and again.
To the worshipful, worshipful of the worshipful, sole cause of all worship; to the eternal, of non-eternal form, sole cause of eternal and non-eternal;
to the eternal even among the eternal, salutation to the most eternal. To the powerful, of the form of power, sole cause of all power;
to the powerful even among the powerful, salutation to the most powerful. To the pure, the all-pure, sole cause of all purity;
to Time, of the form of Time, sole cause of all times; to the Time even of times, salutation to you, the utmost Time.
To the one whose body is all mantras, sole cause of all mantras; to the mantra even of mantras, salutation to the supreme mantra.
To the immeasurable great lord, to Ishana, salutation again and again; to Yoga, of the form of yoga, Person of yoga, salutation to you.
Salutation to you of one throat, of two throats, of many throats; to the one possessed of countless throats, salutation to you, Nilakantha.
Salutation to you, the endless, the great lord, the destroyer and the maker. Salutation to you, Mahadeva; salutation to you, Sadashiva;
salutation to you, supremely pure; salutation to you, salutation again and again. Salutation to the one smeared with ash; salutation to the bearer of the khatvanga;
salutation to you, the self of all; to the lord of the universe salutation again and again. Salutation to you, the all-knowing; to the protector salutation again and again.
Salutation to you, the unmanifest; to the eternal salutation again and again. Salutation to you who dwell on Kailasa; salutation to you who dwell in Patala.
By you all this is pervaded, Lokaloka with the moving and unmoving; even in a thousand years who would be able to praise you?"
Whoever praises the supreme Lord with this divine hymn shakes off all sins and is honoured in Rudra's world.
Tell me all this, great sage, as I ask. Markandeya said: Listen, O king, to a divine and unsurpassed story, worthy of heaven,
hearing which one is freed from all sins by bathing at the holy place. Yayati by name, righteous-souled, devoted to truth and dharma,
an emperor, best of kings, best of all upholders of dharma, sacrificed with great sacrifices like another Shatakratu
where the holy river Madhumati meets the Reva; there a sacrifice was begun with priests and brahmins.
There is the linga Madhyeshvara, Maheshvara the self-existent god; those who bathe there go to heaven, and those who die there are not reborn.
There Madhu and Kaitabha were slain by Vishnu with his discus; by worshipping that god one gains the fruit of a thousand cows.
By the gift of sesame water and pindas, O Bharata, one's ancestors are satisfied for as long as fourteen Indras reign.
There the sacrifice was begun leaving out Hari and Shankara; the daitya Jatasura, seeing the weak point, came there.
Then the sacrifice was destroyed by danavas proud of their strength; the sacrificial posts and vessels were flung in the ten directions;
the offered purodasha was eaten and the soma drunk by them; all the gods vanished out of fear of the danavas.
A hundred and eight gods went away in the form of deer; the giver of wealth vanished in the form of a yaksha and went to his own city;
Dharmaraja mounted on a buffalo, Shatakratu on an elephant, the bearer of oblations on a ram — they went out, keeping their vows.
Varuna too, who had come, vanished and went to his own city on his makara seat, and Vayu took refuge on a deer.
Ishana in the form of the lord fled mounted on the bull; the weapons of the world-guardians were seized by the Danu-born.
Mounting my vehicle alone, how shall I go away with my wife? Reflecting thus, the best of kings seized a weapon, O Bharata,
and said to the unassailable lion of the daityas, "Stand, stand! Those born of a kshatriya family never flee on seeing a foe."

Your forebears were turned back for ten or twelve years. Rudra was not invited here, nor was a share assigned to Rudra;
skandapuran:70:19	in this sacrifice the Person of sacrifice, blessed Hari, was not invited; through that fault my sacrifice has been destroyed by the danavas.
Having said this, the best of kings meditated on Rudra Maheshvara, assumed a fierce form, with the twang of the bowstring roaring,
seized a sword in wrath and slew the danavas. And all the gods headed by Brahma were invited again.
The gods spoke to the king, O Bharata: "There has been no one equal to you here, royal sage, nor will there be."
Hearing the gods' words, Yayati said: "The sacrifice has been set going again by the grace of Hara and Vishnu;
flight is not proper for a kshatriya here." By that deed the trident-handed bearer of Pinaka was praised,
and a linga rose there from Patala, bright as the fire of doom; the whole world was made white by its radiance, O Bharata.
The bull-bannered one said to him, "Choose a boon — blessings on you." Yayati said: "If you are pleased with me, god, and wish to give me a boon,
do not leave this place, Shankara, together with Uma; and let sacrifice, gifts and all else done here be imperishable always.
Men without austerity, without giving and full of sin — let them all go to your city by the power of Shuklatirtha."
Mahadeva said to him: "What you have spoken shall be true; whatever desire a man desires, he obtains it,
by the greatness of this holy place and the worship of this linga; they never see hell in birth after birth, O Bharata."
This I have told you, O king, as spoken by Skanda and Shiva; the daityas slain there too reached Shiva's abode.
Mounting each his own vehicle, the gods went to heaven; filled with supreme joy and praised, the best of kings,
the royal sage named Yayati, having ruled his kingdom, went to heaven. By hearing and reciting this one is honoured in Shiva's world.
By seeing, touching and worshipping the god Diptadeva, dreadful sin gathered over many births perishes in a moment.
The man who worships for a single day, or even a muhurta, has no return to the dreadful ocean of worldly existence.
Know Chamunda named Mokshada to be Gauri and Sarasvati. He was praised with a thousand names by Vishnu and by Brahma himself.
The lingas praised on the northern bank of the Reva are Omkara, Adhideva, Bilvamraka Maheshvara,
Shukleshvara, Bhrigu, Dvipeshvara and Trilochana. When the Vaivasvata Manvantara had come, in the first kalpa, in the Krita age,
the lord of Shri was the first and supreme, the second the Grandsire, the third the king of the gods, the fourth the Sun,
the fifth is declared the Moon, the sixth proclaimed Rahu, the seventh Shani, the eighth remembered as Ketu,
the ninth Vaishvanara, the tenth the lord of the directions, the eleventh Vaikrama, the twelfth Varuna,
the thirteenth Vayu and the fourteenth the giver of wealth. In various verbal forms the god, husband of Uma, was praised
by Vishnu lord of the gods, by Brahma and by gods and asuras: Steady, Sthanu, Radiant Sun, Foremost, Boon-giver, Excellent,
Hari, the one called Harina, Remover of all beings, Lord, Activity and Cessation, Restraint, Eternal, Fixed,
Dweller in the cremation ground, the Blessed One, Sky-goer and Earth-goer, Worthy of salutation, of great deeds, Ascetic, Creator of beings,
Hidden in the guise of a madman, Lord of creatures of all worlds, of great form, of great body, Lord of creatures of all worlds,
Supreme self of all beings, Misshapen, Dwarf, Manu, World-guardian, of concealed self, Gracious, Destroyer of existence,
Active, of great limbs, the Accumulation, of fixed support, All-desire, Self-born, Maker of the beginning and the beginningless, Treasure,
Thousand-eyed, Odd-eyed, Soma, Accomplisher of the stars, Moon, Sun, Shani, Ketu, Planet, Lord of planets, Excellent,
Seer of austerity, Strength, the Abiding, Archer at the deer, Sinless, of great austerity, of long austerity, the First, Compassionate to the wretched,
Maker of the year, Mantra, the Measure, supreme Austerity, Yogi, of the great might of yoga, of great seed, Hara the Remover,
Great-minded, All-knowing, With seed, Remover, Hara, Bearer of the water-pot, Bowman, with life in his hand, Majestic,
the Portion, without a master, Trident-bearer, bearer of the khatvanga and the pattisha, Pure, of pure form, Radiance, Maker of radiance, Treasure,
Turbaned, Fair-faced, Udakya, Vitana, Hari, Tawny-eyed, of good fords, and Krishna,
of jackal form, All-purposed, Shundi, Pure, the Water-pot, Unborn, Garlanded with fragrance, of deer form, Skull-bearer,

of lion and tiger form, Wearer of the wet hide, Hara, Yogi of time, of great roar, dwelling in all, the Crossroads,
Mover among irresistible ghosts, Mover among beings, Maheshvara, Manifold being, of much wealth, All-purposed, the lovely Goal,
Fond of dance, Maker of dance, Dancer, the Cloud, Dreadful, of great austerity, the Dwelling, Eternal, Bearer of the mountain, the Sky,
of a thousand beings, to be known, Resolve and Certainty, Impatience and Patience, Daksha, Destroyer of Daksha's sacrifice,
Carrier-off of Daksha's sacrifice, very great, the Middle, Taker of radiance, Slayer of Bali, Joyful, Worshipped, Bhava,
of deep voice, Deep, Profound, Bearer of oblations, of banyan form, of the colour of the banyan and the bear, Lord, All-pervading,
of sharp arrows, Tawny-eyed, the great Lord, Knower of the time of rites, Consecration, the Propitiated, Sacrifice, Ocean, Submarine fire,
Eater of oblations, whose mouth is fire, of serene self, Fire, of great radiance, of good radiance, Victory and Conquest,
Course of the luminaries, Success, Union and Division, Crested, Staff-bearer, Matted-haired, Flaming, Murtoda, Weak, the Outside,
Bearer of the bamboo, Vetala to sin, Fire of doom, Staff of death, whose body is the stars, Growth, the Unborn, Bearer of fragrance, the First-born,

of the nature of space, the Descent, the Serpent, Khala, of fierce form, Sun among gods, with rays of wealth, of good lustre,

the Maddened, of the form of Madana, the great Maker of gain and loss, of perfected yoga, the Remover, the Perfected, Accomplisher of all aims,
the Mendicant, of mendicant form, Lord of the six, of soft skin, Mahasena, Vishakha, Yashtibhaga, Lord of cows,

Nandishvara, Sunandi, Nandana, Increaser of joy, wearing serpents as a necklace, the Sportive, Time, best of knowers of Brahman,

Husband of Uma, Beloved of Uma, Bearer of Jahnavi, Steadfast, Excellent, All-purposed, the Purpose of all beings, Eternal, of all vows, Pure.

The god who is not known by Brahma and the gods nor by the great sages — how can he be praised, lord, the supreme self, beyond the highest?
skandapuran:71:55	Forgive the fickleness of our tongues, supreme Lord; bring welfare to the gods and increase the prosperity of the dwellers in heaven.
Markandeya said: Hearing this hymn, the glorious god Dvipeshvara, Shiva, was pleased and said to the gods: "Ask for a boon, gods."
The gods said: "If the great Lord, the lord who grants boons to the gods, is pleased, then be our protector and destroy the daityas, Maheshvara.
And let even the vilest doer of evil who worships the five lingas attain that goal which is hard to reach even by great sacrifices."
There long ago the god of gods, husband of Uma, saluted by gods and asuras, surrounded by Shakra, was praised with a thousand names;
thereafter the king of the gods was endowed with Shiva's grace. There the lord god Lakshmeshvara was praised by the giver of wealth.
Know that goddess, Gauri named Mokshada, O Bharata, and the Siddhalinga Moksheshvara, saluted by gods and asuras.
Siddhas, vidyadharas, yakshas, gandharvas, kinnaras and men attained divinity by worshipping the five lingas.
Kubera, Maruta, Varuna and Nirriti, Vaivasvata Yama and then the lord of hell —
by the greatness of that linga the greatly famous son of the Sun rose high. Formerly the lord Dvipeshvara was praised there by others;
Shiva, the most worshipful, was praised with devotion with a thousand names; hence the Moon became an ornament on Shambhu's head there.
Gauri was worshipped by Rohini, and so she became fortunate; likewise the Pinaka-bearing god was praised by the stars joined in yoga,
and so by them and by the sun the sky was adorned. The diseases, Kala and Mrityu, and Chitragupta the scribe —
so too the lord Shakra was surrounded by these hosts of gods; he is most dreadful to the sinful and gracious to the righteous.
Eight crores with bristling hair, fierce and with deformed faces; and with thousands of chaste wives and those who fasted for a month,
with cries of "kilkila", the excellent city of Dharmaraja was filled all around by countless glorious and lovely ones.
Hearing their clamour, Dharmaraja with his courtiers, clad in white garments, with white garlands and unguents,
went quickly on foot to where they stood in their vehicles; with joined palms he asked those doers of good deeds:
By what discipline, according to your ability, did you practise the great dharma surpassing dharma? From what land have you come? How was your merit earned?
Those mounted on the vehicles said: "Austerity was performed at Kurukshetra and especially on the Ganga; that is established as the door to all worlds.
Dharma and adharma are in truth your strength and cause. Varanasi, Prayaga, the meeting of the Ganga and the ocean,
the most holy Pitritirtha, Pushkara and Naimisha, Kedara, Bhairava and Rudramahalaya,
Sarasvati, Rudrakoti, Prabhasa and Shashibhushana — at thousands of holy places gifts, sacrifice and austerity were performed.
This we have told you in full, greatly famous son of the Sun." Others, seeing Dharmaraja as was fitting, then likewise
all spoke gentle words to Dharmaraja, as follows: "You are not the lord of those who do good; Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva are their lord.
Of those devoted to sinful deeds Yama himself is the ruler." Yama said: "Wait until I go to Kailasa and return."
Having said this, O king, he went to Kailasa, best of mountains, where Shiva and all the others were, and Parvati and Shanmukha.
All the gods were praising the god of gods, husband of Uma; some danced before him, leaping up and falling down.
Seeing Shambhu thus, of blazing radiance, amid the praises, praising the god of gods, the Pinaka-bearer, with a thousand names,
and prostrating with eight limbs, Dharmaraja said this: "Those who have come to our city — what goal is declared for them?"
Laughing, the god said to Dharmaraja, Yudhishthira: "Let all those who dwell on the bank of the Reva come here;
let those who dwell at other holy places enjoy pleasures in heaven." Then hearing Shiva's word as it was, Brahma and Vishnu
and the lord of all the hosts of gods were satisfied with the god's word; in a moment Dharmaraja came back to his excellent city.
All those named by Shiva were sent to Shiva's world, Yudhishthira, and the others too, possessed of good, as they had been directed.
I saw this in a former kalpa, at the coming of the gods on the full moon of Kartika. Then one should go, great king, to the excellent Vaishnava holy place
renowned as Kokila, which releases from all sins; Janardana, god of gods, called it a Vaishnava field.
A crore and a quarter of holy places are there, O Bharata. Having fasted on the holy eleventh day one should light a row of lamps;
he has no return to the hard-to-bear mortal world, going in the foremost of vehicles rich in all desires, O Bharata.
The ancestors' satisfaction lasts for countless ages, no doubt; when a brahmin is gratified there, the gift is beyond counting.
Whoever gives up life here, helplessly or willingly, becomes a king in the city of the vidyadharas for ten thousand years.
Dhruva attained the status of the pole in heaven, blazing with the radiance of the stars; and other hosts of beings born in mortal wombs,
worshipping the god of gods, attained divinity in heaven. When the gods' merit is exhausted they become mortals, and by devotion and merit mortals become gods;
this distinction of heaven and the mortal world comes from the distinction of dharma and adharma. By some means or other Maheshvara is to be worshipped;
whatever it may be, it should be offered to Shiva with a mind full of devotion. By Arundhati, by Bharani, and by Savitri likewise,
by Ahalya, Menaka, Marutvati and Rambha, by throngs of apsarases and by hosts of gods and siddhas —
whoever has worshipped Shankara resorting to the bank of the Narmada has obtained abundant enjoyments and liberation, O Bharata.
Whoever, deluded by Shiva's maya, does not worship Hara has neither heaven nor liberation — what then to speak of Kailasa?
Nor is he a vessel for heaven or kingship, lord of men. The Reva contains all holy places and Hara contains all gods;
the understanding contains all dharma; austerity consists of patience and truth; celibacy is the root of austerity, and the restraint of the five senses;
patience, truth, japa, study — austerity is marked by self-control. This I have told you, O king, as it was told by Shiva long ago,
and by me to you, king of kings, and especially to your brothers; the goddess I have told you of is no ordinary one.
Dvipeshvara, Kapileshvara and Narakeshvara — rising early, one should duly glorify these gods;
obtaining the fruit of all holy places, one is honoured in Shiva's world. When the flood of sin is exhausted, the river flowing through seven kalpas is reached,
in which Shiva is present; therefore it is the supreme field of Shiva. By hearing and reciting this, one is honoured in Shiva's world.
Everything given and offered here becomes imperishable. Most wonderful, great king, are bathing in the Narmada and worship there.
Many thousands of aerial cars, Yudhishthira, equal to crores of suns with their nets of radiance from many gems,
went to the city of Dharmaraja with the sound of vinas and the like, making heaven and earth resound with the roar of Vedic chanting.
At one time King Vaivasvata saw this wonder, as did Atri, Vasishtha, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu,
these seven sages and the others, judges of dharma and adharma, installed long ago by Shiva, Hari and Brahma.
Yudhishthira said: "How does a man whose bonds of karma are not exhausted attain the supreme state, best of sages? Tell me that, you who live through the kalpas."
Markandeya said: It was told long ago by Vishnu to the great-souled Brahma: "I take refuge in the lotus-eyed god Narayana, Hari,
lord of the world, thousand-eyed, the imperishable, the supreme state; I take refuge in the Blessed One, lord of past, future and present,
creator of all beings, of endless strength and valour; I take refuge in Padmanabha, Hrishikesha, the true, the imperishable.
Hiranyagarbha, womb of the earth, immortal, facing all sides, undying and without a master — I take refuge in the one with the sun's lustre.
The thousand-headed god, Vaikuntha, borne by Garuda — I take refuge in the subtle, the unmoving, the most excellent giver of fearlessness.
Narayana and Hari, whose self is yoga, the eternal, refuge of all worlds — I take refuge in the steadfast Lord.
He who is lord of all beings, by whom all this is pervaded, the god who brings dissolution — may that Vishnu be gracious to me.
From whom long ago Brahma, the lotus-born Prajapati, was born — may that Vishnu, the lord beyond the Grandsire, be gracious to me.
When dissolution came long ago and the world of moving and unmoving perished, the one whose self is yoga remained alone — may that Vishnu be gracious to me.
He who is the earth, truth, time, dharma and the fruit of action, bearing the form of the hosts — may Vasudeva, the object of those words, be gracious.
Salutation to you, abode of yoga, abode of all, giver of boons; enjoyer of sacrifice, enjoyer of the five, Narayana, salutation to you.
Four-formed one, abode of the world, abode of Lakshmi, giver of boons, abode of the universe, salutation to you, witness, lord of the world.
Unconquerable, the one universal form of six divisions, Vrishakapi, lord of beasts and Time — salutation to you, ocean of knowledge.
From the unmanifest arose the egg, and from the unmanifest the other lord; beyond whom there is nothing higher — to him I have gone for refuge.
The lord on whom Brahma, Ishana and the rest ever meditate, who, all-pervading, stands supporting the whole world with a single portion,
ungraspable, without qualities, the ruler — to him I have gone for refuge. He who stands like a light between the sun and the moon,
whom they call the knower of the field — may that great-souled one be gracious. The other perfected ones and great sages who through Sankhya and yoga
are freed by knowing him — may that great-souled one be gracious. Salutation to you, auspicious on all sides, with eyes, heads and faces everywhere;
salutation to you, the changeless, the first cause, dwelling in the heart; salutation to you, beyond the senses; supreme self, salutation to you.
Those who know you do not dwell in worldly existence; they are freed from attachment and hatred and rid of greed and delusion.
Bodiless and well hidden, you pervade all bodies; the unmanifest, intellect, ego, the great elements and the senses —
they are in you, you are not in them; they are not you, nor are you they. Unmanifest, not merely immutable, lord of the gunas, the Lord,
the round of existence, its cause and its end, the lord abiding in his own self — salutation to you, lotus-eyed; Vasudeva, salutation to you.
You are the Lord, lord of the world; what higher can be said? You are the giver of liberation to devotees, the guru and lord of the thirty gods.
You are my lord of beings, my master in birth after birth, whether I am bound by ego or by the gunas beginning with sattva.
Let my smell go to earth, my taste to water, my sight to fire, my touch to the wind,
sound to space, and the mind likewise to its cause; my ego to the intellect, and let my intellect rest in you.
May I be separated from all instruments, gunas and elements; may sattva, rajas and tamas enter their own prakriti.
I, a man, take refuge in the faultless lord, lord of lords, the thousand-headed god, the great sage, creator of beings,
the source of Brahma and of the universe — may that Vishnu be gracious to me. When the moving and unmoving perish, they dissolve into Brahma's consort;
at the great deluge the Mahat dissolves into prakriti, and it is poured forth again from those two — may that Vishnu be gracious to me.
He who surpasses the radiances of Agni, Soma, the sun and the gods, of Brahma, Rudra, Indra and the yogis — may that Vishnu be gracious to me.
You are unborn, the path of the world, formless and the conqueror of the universal form; Pradhana, Mahat, the Person, the conscious and the inert —
he who is beyond these, not to be concealed — to him alone I have gone for refuge. He who himself sends down the radiance like the moon and sun,
from whom the directions are born — may that great-souled one be gracious. With qualities and without qualities, conscious and unconscious, self-moving,
subtle, all-pervading, embodied — may that great-souled one be gracious. The moon stands within the sun, and he is remembered as in its midst;
he who, being all beings, is unmoving and shining — may that great-souled one be gracious. Those who know your manifoldness through your oneness go to the Supreme.
Equal to all beings, neither hostile nor partial to his own, he worships equally without desire, and is worshipped by those whose minds are on nothing else;
he who is to be known with the whole self — may that Vishnu be gracious to me. All this moving and unmoving, the fourfold host of beings,
is strung on you like threads, like clusters of gems on a string. You have neither dharma nor adharma, neither womb nor birth again.
For release from old age and birth I have gone to him alone for refuge. The senses and the gunas, the in-breath and out-breath in the wombs,
the body, merely like wood and perishable, which is the supreme calamity, my solitary state from birth, and rebirth here —
with my mind on you, my breath gone to you, your devotee, wholly devoted to you, I shall remember you alone when death is at hand.
Let the diseases earned in a former body enter me, and the pains of wind and the rest; release me from that debt, lord.
The highest good among good things and among other glorious ones, for the purification of all sins, holy, which is the supreme state —
rising at dawn continually, at midday and at day's end, it should be recited unceasingly, granting the calming of all sins:

I bow to Hari, Krishna, Hrishikesha, Vasudeva, Janardana, lord of the world — may he remove my sin.

For the royal sage named Nabhaga, at the confluence on the bank of the Narmada — this incomparable Vaishnava hymn was made by Prajapati;
it was received from Brahma by Angiras, and from him by Indra, O Bharata; Vasishtha recited it to Nabhaga, best of kings.
Having bathed in the water of the Narmada and given many gifts, Nabhaga mounted a vehicle that went at will and went to his own city.
Whoever praises Janardana with this hymn of a thousand names has no return to the dreadful ocean of worldly existence.
Long ago in the Treta age, dear one, the descendant of Pulastya, thorn of the gods, conqueror of the three worlds, fierce, terror of gods and asuras,
unslayable by gods, danavas, yakshas, gandharvas, serpents and rakshasas by virtue of a boon, was roaming the earth.
There on the lovely Devagiri lived a danava proud of his strength, renowned as Maya, a great one, lord of kings.
Ravana went to him and stood bowed in humility; honoured with gifts and respect, he said to Maya:
Whose is this lotus-eyed maiden with a face like the full moon? What is her name, and why does she practise fierce austerity, lord?
Maya said: "I am Maya by name, the chief lord of the danavas; my wife is named Tejavati, and this lovely one is my daughter,
renowned as Mandodari; she practises austerity for the sake of a husband." Hearing his words, Ravana, proud and intoxicated,
grew courteous, bowed and said to Maya: "I am the king called Paulastya, crusher of the pride of gods and danavas;
I ask, fortunate one — you should give me your daughter." Knowing him to be of the Grandsire's line, the great-souled Maya
gave his daughter to Ravana according to rule. Taking her then, the rakshasa, honoured by the night-rovers,
sported with her in divine vehicles and aerial cars; that best of those blessed with sons begot a son, O Bharata.
As soon as he was born, the great-souled one let out a roar like that of the cloud of dissolution, by which the world was stunned.
Hearing that dreadful roar, the Grandsire of the world was frightened and then named him: "He shall be Meghanada."
Having received this name, he undertook a supreme vow and meditated on the lord of gods, Shankara with Uma,
with vows, restraints, gifts, oblations and japa according to rule; his body was worn down by divine krichchhras and chandrayanas.
Then on another day, dear one, he went to Kailasa, upholder of the earth, obtained the linga and set out facing south.
Resorting to the bank of the Narmada, the mighty one, wishing to bathe, set it down, did japa and worshipped the god, lord of people.
Wishing to go on by the further road to Lanka, best of kings, he lifted up one linga, held in his left hand —
the first and the second, with devotion, the son of Paulastya — and then the great linga of the god fell into the water of the Narmada.
Protect me, protect me, he cried to the supreme linga; meanwhile the second fell on the northern bank of the Narmada.
The lovely linga there is renowned as Meghanada; the one named Madhyameshvara stands in the midst of the water.
While he wished to lift it out, it went down to the seven netherworlds; knowing the resolve of the two gods, the night-rover turned back
and went off, entering the sky, honoured by the night-rovers. From that time the holy place has been renowned as Meghanada,
also renowned as Megharava; on the north is the auspicious Khetaka, and on the east the one named Garjana, which destroys all sins.
Whoever bathes at that holy place, king of kings, and stays there a day and a night, obtains eternal good.
Whoever offers pindas at that holy place, lord of men, satisfies his ancestors in heaven for twelve years.
Whoever feeds brahmins at that holy place, lord of men, obtains there the fruit of yogis, no doubt.
Entering fire or water there, or fasting to death — his goal is one of no return; so said Shankara.
